advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make tracker-maintenance actually remove COMMITTED foreign paths (commit the deletion, e.g. via commit_and_push_tickets_branch) or clearly report them as still-committed rather than 'removed'.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/tracker_maintenance.py:238: `_git(tracker, "rm", "-r", "-q", "--cached", "--ignore-unmatch", "--", name)` — index-only removal, no subsequent commit anywhere in the function (search for 'commit' finds only docstring/labels)

src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py:522: `probe = run_git(tracker, "cat-file", "-e", f"HEAD:{top}", check=False)` — path_is_foreign_to_branch keys off HEAD, so a committed foreign path stays 'committed' after an uncommitted rm --cached
src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py:457: `f" {len(committed)} of them are COMMITTED to the tickets branch ... and will propagate on the next push."` — the case the repair fails to actually clear
src/rebar/_commands/tracker_maintenance.py:262: `f"repaired: {len(stranded)} stranded, {len(foreign)} foreign path(s) removed\n"` — reports removal that did not durably happen for committed paths
advisory.finding: For a foreign top-level path that is COMMITTED to the tickets branch, the repair does `git rm --cached ... --ignore-unmatch` plus a worktree delete but never commits the removal, so the path remains in HEAD/branch history. fsck (via path_is_foreign_to_branch, which checks `cat-file -e HEAD:<top>`) will still report it as committed and it will still propagate on the next push — yet the command prints 'repaired' and records it under foreign_paths as removed.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Use init_only=True (or a no-sync path) for the tracker-maintenance arm so it inspects the existing store without triggering a reconverge/reset before the safety envelope runs.
evidence: src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:345: `ensure_initialized(init_only=False)`
src/rebar/_cli/_init.py:193: `if init_only:` / `return` — full mode falls through to ensure_fresh
src/rebar/_cli/_init.py:201: `reads.ensure_fresh(reads.tracker_dir(repo_root))`

src/rebar/_engine_support/reads.py:190: docstring: 'throttled ... fetch + reconverge of the local tickets branch with origin/tickets ... merge-as-union, lock-guarded reset' — a store mutation run before maintenance inspects the wedged store
src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:342: comment 'must never auto-init one — an operator reaching for maintenance is repairing an EXISTING store'
advisory.finding: The dispatch arm calls ensure_initialized(init_only=False), whose full mode runs reads.ensure_fresh — a fetch + merge-as-union + lock-guarded reset that MUTATES the tracker — before tracker_maintenance inspects it. This contradicts the arm's own comment ('repairing an EXISTING store') and the command's 'no writes before the guard' design, and can alter the stranded-index / unpushed-commits state the envelope is meant to protect.
advisory.suggested_fix: Route the arm through ensure_initialized(init_only=True) (matching the read-only inspect intent), or resolve the tracker directly without ensure_fresh.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test where the foreign path is committed to the tickets branch and assert the branch no longer carries it after --clean (and that fsck stops reporting it).
evidence: tests/interfaces/store/test_tracker_maintenance_2fa6.py:47: `(tracker / "src").mkdir()` and `(tracker / "src" / "leak.py").write_text(...)` occur after the clone with no _commit call — a working-tree stray only
tests/interfaces/store/test_tracker_maintenance_2fa6.py:82: `assert audit[0]["foreign_paths"] == ["src"]` — asserts removal only for the uncommitted stray
advisory.finding: No test covers the committed-foreign-path repair. The fixture creates `src/leak.py` AFTER cloning and never commits it, so every test exercises only the working-tree-stray branch; the 'strictly worse' committed case (which the repair does not durably fix) is untested.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that seeds an unmerged/stranded index entry and asserts tracker-maintenance --clean heals it (exercises discard_unmerged_paths and the regenerable/stranded_foreign split).
evidence: Fixture only pollutes with foreign paths: tracker/test:55-56 '(tracker / "src").mkdir(); (tracker / "src" / "leak.py").write_text(...)'
No test creates an unmerged index entry; every assertion targets foreign paths e.g. test:101 'assert audit[0]["foreign_paths"] == ["src"]' and test:96 'assert not (tracker / "src").exists()'

Source repair branch untested: src/rebar/_commands/tracker_maintenance.py:234-236 'regenerable = [p for p in stranded ...]; stranded_foreign = [...]; discard_unmerged_paths(tracker, regenerable, stranded_foreign)'
Module docstring names the stranded index as the target: tracker_maintenance.py _stranded_paths docstring 'Paths left unmerged in the index (the state that blocks every ticket write).'
advisory.finding: The stranded/unmerged-index repair path is never exercised by any test. Every test uses a fixture that only creates a foreign top-level tree ('src/leak.py'), so _stranded_paths() returns [] in all runs and the entire heal branch — the regenerable/stranded_foreign split and discard_unmerged_paths() at lines 234-236 — never executes. This is the command's primary reason to exist (the incident 'left the index with unmerged entries and no MERGE_HEAD, and blocked every ticket write'), yet a regression that broke unmerged-path healing would pass the whole suite.
scenarios: A regression in discard_unmerged_paths call args or the regenerable/foreign classification would ship undetected
The report count 'stranded index entries : N' is only ever verified as 0
advisory.suggested_fix: Extend the fixture (or add a variant) that produces an unmerged index entry (e.g. via a conflicting merge in the tracker worktree), then assert --clean reports it under 'stranded index entries', discards it, and records it in audit['stranded_paths'].

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] In the break-glass test, also assert the foreign tree was removed (e.g. `assert not (tracker / 'src').exists()`) and a backup ref was written.
evidence: test_break_glass_overrides_the_refusal_and_is_recorded asserts only audit fields: test:141-144 'assert len(audit) == 1; assert audit[0]["forced"] is True; ... assert audit[0]["unpushed_commits"] == 1'
No assertion that (tracker / 'src') was removed after the forced run, unlike test_clean_takes_the_backup_ref_then_repairs test:96
advisory.finding: The break-glass repair test asserts the audit record but never asserts the repair actually happened under --force. It checks forced/reason/unpushed_commits in the audit line but not that the foreign 'src' tree was removed, so a bug where --force records the override but skips the actual mutation would pass.
scenarios: A force path that logs the override but returns before running the foreign-removal loop would go undetected

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that forces backup-ref creation to fail (or an unreachable git dir) and asserts rc==2 with no mutation.
evidence: Untested rc-2 path: tracker_maintenance.py:229-231 'if backup_ref is None: sys.stderr.write("Error: could not create the backup ref — refusing to mutate.\n"); return 2'
Untested audit fallback: tracker_maintenance.py:265 'sys.stdout.write(f"audit: {audit or \'(could not write audit log)\'}\n")'
No test in the suite triggers a None backup_ref or a None audit path.
advisory.finding: The backup-ref-creation-failure path (returns exit 2, 'could not create the backup ref — refusing to mutate') and the audit-write-failure fallback ('(could not write audit log)') are untested. These are error/edge paths for the safety envelope but have no coverage.
scenarios: If backup-ref creation silently regressed to proceed on failure, no test would catch the missing 'refuse to mutate' guarantee

blocking.finding: bugfix-size-attestation: this change touches 437 non-test line(s) — over the 150-line floor for a bug fix — but bug 2fa6-e3cb-a11f-4e3d has no acceptable plan-review attestation (verdict: unsigned; no plan-review attestation record). A fix this large is a design change wearing a bug label: write the fix plan into the ticket's description, run `rebar review-plan 2fa6-e3cb-a11f-4e3d` (it auto-escalates a bug with non-test file impact to the full review and SIGNS an attestation on a PASS; if the review passed but no attestation landed, `rebar sign-review 2fa6-e3cb-a11f-4e3d` re-persists it cheaply, and `rebar review-plan 2fa6-e3cb-a11f-4e3d --status` confirms it is current without an LLM call), then re-push.
